method: The evaluation framework uses two independent computational paths to ensure no data leakage. The Predicted Path processes a 2D input image through the VLM (Gemini), which extracts a structured 3D scene JSON. Post-hoc scale calibration corrects dimensional error using one reference dimension (the longest horizontal span). The calibrated scene is then automatically meshed and solved using OpenFOAM to produce the predicted CFD solution. The Reference Path starts from the rule-based benchmark generator, which produces the ground-truth scene JSON directly without any VLM involvement. The ground-truth scene is used for two purposes: (1) it is rendered into 2D images that serve as inputs to the VLM in the predicted path, and (2) it is independently meshed and solved using the same OpenFOAM pipeline to produce the reference CFD solution. Critically, the reference path does not involve any VLM invocation. The 2D renderings are used only as VLM inputs and do not participate in the reference CFD computation. Both paths converge at the Metric Comparison stage, which computes structural similarity scores (geometric fidelity) and reference CFD agreement scores (flow-field accuracy) by comparing the predicted and reference solutions on a common normalised lattice. This separation ensures that the evaluation is free from circular reasoning or data leakage.
caption: Evaluation pathway showing data-leakage prevention. The predicted path (top) processes the 2D input through VLM, scale calibration, and CFD. The reference path (bottom) generates the ground-truth CFD solution from the rule-based benchmark geometry without VLM involvement. Both paths converge at the metric comparison stage, which produces structural and reference CFD agreement scores.
